definitions.explanation: Taking a photo or filming a scene again because the first attempt was unsatisfactory.

examples.japanese: {写真|しゃしん}の{撮|と}り{直|なお}しをお{願|ねが}いした。
examples.english: I asked for a retake of the photo.

examples.japanese: {目|め}をつぶってしまったので{撮|と}り{直|なお}しになった。
examples.english: I blinked, so we had to retake it.

examples.japanese: {監督|かんとく}は{何度|なんど}も{撮|と}り{直|なお}しを{要求|ようきゅう}して、スタッフが{疲|つか}れ{切|き}っていた。
examples.english: The director demanded retakes over and over, and the staff were exhausted.

notes:
{撮|と}り{直|なお}し is the noun form of the verb {撮|と}り{直|なお}す (to retake, to reshoot). It follows the common ～{直|なお}し pattern meaning "re-doing" something.

FORMS:
{撮|と}る (to take a photo/film) + {直|なお}す (to redo) → {撮|と}り{直|なお}し (a retake)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {撮|と}り{直|なお}しを{頼|たの}む: to ask for a retake
- {撮|と}り{直|なお}しになる: to result in a retake
- {何度|なんど}も{撮|と}り{直|なお}し: many retakes

USAGE:
Used for both casual photography (redoing a snapshot) and professional film/video production. In film contexts, retakes can number in the dozens for demanding directors.

SIMILAR ～{直|なお}し WORDS:
- {書|か}き{直|なお}し: rewrite
- {作|つく}り{直|なお}し: remaking
- やり{直|なお}し: redo, start over
